svg.title: How a dry-run and a run share one plan
svg.desc: The planners read the documents, the trash and the tasks of Paperless, the inbox and the archive in Nextcloud, and the states in the database, and change none of them. They plan one action at a time for each document and file, such as an export, a move, a move to the deleted folder, a deletion or an upload, when it fits the batch, and leave it for a later run otherwise. In a run, the executor makes the change and saves the state; in a dry-run, it changes nothing. Both report the same line and take the same place in the batch, so the plan of the next document sees the batch as it stands: in a run, a failed export frees its place, and a full quota stops the other writes.
